newsitem.title: FRANCE: France reports more bids for EU wheat exports.
newsitem.headline: France reports more bids for EU wheat exports.

text.p: Grain traders bid through France on Wednesday for licences to export 140,000 tonnes of soft wheat at a fixed daily tax of three Ecus per tonne, the cereals authority ONIC said.
Traders also bid for 28,000 tonnes of soft wheat flour at an export tax of four Ecus per tonne.
The bids bring to 417,500 tonnes the known quantity of soft wheat grain sought by the trade since the European Commission on Tuesday rejected a previous round of bids for a million tonnes.

The Commission said on Wednesday it would make no immediate decision on the 277,500 tonnes which had been sought through France on Tuesday, but that if too many further bids arrived all the oustanding applications would be quickly rejected.
The Commission has not said what volume of wheat exports it regards as acceptable, drawing criticism from some traders who say it has left them without a clear idea of its intentions.
The EU's executive must decide within three working days whether to use its power of veto to reject each export bid.
